risk_of_bias_reason: 6 of 12 trials at high overall risk of bias (unconcealed allocation, unblinded outcome assessment); ascertainment of NEC can be influenced by knowledge of feeding allocation
indirectness_reason: Population, intervention and outcome definition directly applicable
imprecision_reason: Only 38 events in 3,160 infants; 95% CI spans a 58% relative reduction to a 71% relative increase, i.e. both appreciable benefit and appreciable harm
publication_bias_reason: Egger p = 0.86; no asymmetry, but most trials small and single-centre so bias cannot be excluded
comments: No evidence that withholding parenteral nutrition and feeding fully from birth increases NEC, but the analysis cannot exclude a clinically important increase or decrease. This is the outcome the review was principally designed to address and it remains the key evidence gap.

risk_of_bias_reason: Death is an objective outcome not susceptible to detection bias; no downgrade despite allocation-concealment limitations in several trials
imprecision_reason: 77 events in 2,701 infants; 95% CI 0.68 to 1.54 includes both a 32% relative reduction and a 54% relative increase in mortality
comments: No signal of a mortality difference in either direction; the confidence interval remains too wide to establish equivalence.

risk_of_bias_reason: 6 of 12 trials at high overall risk of bias; blood-culture sampling thresholds are clinician-driven and unblinded
inconsistency_reason: I² = 50%, Q p = 0.051; a credible setting effect is present (RR 0.44 in lower-middle-income trials vs 1.00 in the single high-income trial, subgroup difference p < 0.05), so the pooled estimate averages across genuinely different effects
indirectness_reason: Directly applicable, although baseline sepsis risk differs greatly between settings
imprecision_reason: 148 events; 95% CI 0.35 to 1.15 crosses the null and includes a 65% relative reduction
publication_bias_reason: Egger p = 0.076 on 8 trials; test underpowered and confounded by real heterogeneity
comments: The most plausible mechanism of benefit is avoidance of central venous catheters and parenteral nutrition. The pooled estimate is not significant, but the effect is concentrated in lower-middle-income settings where baseline sepsis risk and catheter-associated risk are highest; readers should use the subgroup estimates rather than the pooled figure.

risk_of_bias_reason: Subjective, clinician-adjudicated outcome assessed without blinding in every trial; 6 of 12 trials at high overall risk of bias
indirectness_reason: Definitions varied widely between trials (gastric residual volume thresholds, abdominal distension, emesis, feed interruption of differing duration), so the pooled effect refers to a composite of related but non-identical constructs
imprecision_reason: 248 events in 1,101 infants; 95% CI 0.54 to 0.95 excludes the null
publication_bias_reason: Egger p = 0.37, Begg-Mazumdar p = 0.24; trim-and-fill moved the estimate further from the null
comments: The one dichotomous outcome showing benefit. The estimate is statistically fragile: it loses conventional significance under the Hartung-Knapp adjustment (p = 0.053) and when any of several individual trials is omitted. Given the unblinded, subjectively defined outcome, part of the effect may reflect differential thresholds for declaring intolerance rather than a true physiological difference.

risk_of_bias_reason: Screening frequency and glucose thresholds were protocol-dependent and not blinded
inconsistency_reason: I² = 45%; the pooled direction reverses (RR 0.80 to RR 1.14) when trials at high risk of bias are excluded
imprecision_reason: Only 69 events in 534 infants; 95% CI 0.37 to 1.75
comments: The theoretical concern that withholding parenteral glucose causes hypoglycaemia is neither confirmed nor refuted. Only six small trials reported it, screening protocols differed, and the direction of effect is unstable.

risk_of_bias_reason: 6 of 12 trials at high overall risk of bias; discharge timing is a clinician decision made with knowledge of allocation
inconsistency_reason: I² = 90%, Q p < 0.001; trial estimates range from about -14 to about 0 days and the risk-of-bias subgroup difference is significant, with the low-risk and some-concerns trials sitting closer to the null
indirectness_reason: Directly applicable, though absolute length of stay differs several-fold between settings
imprecision_reason: 2,506 infants; 95% CI -6.40 to -1.49 days excludes the null and both limits are clinically meaningful
publication_bias_reason: Egger p = 0.084; Sanghvi 2013 lies well outside the funnel and its removal halves the pooled effect
comments: A shorter stay of roughly 4 days is estimated, but heterogeneity is extreme and the effect is largely carried by early, small, high-risk trials from lower-middle-income settings. Under the Hartung-Knapp adjustment the effect is only marginal (p = 0.049) and it is not significant when high-risk trials are excluded.

outcome: Time to attain full enteral feeds (days)
risk_of_bias_reason: 6 of 12 trials at high overall risk of bias; feed advancement was managed unblinded by the treating team
inconsistency_reason: I² = 90%; a credible setting effect is present (subgroup difference p < 0.05) with much larger reductions in lower-middle-income trials
indirectness_reason: The outcome is partly determined by the intervention definition itself: infants allocated to full feeds from birth are at full feed volumes by protocol, so this measure reflects protocol adherence as much as an independent physiological benefit
imprecision_reason: 2,577 infants; 95% CI -3.47 to -1.14 days excludes the null
comments: Earlier attainment of full feeds is the most consistently reported finding, but it is close to tautological given the intervention and should not be treated as an independent patient-important benefit.

risk_of_bias_reason: 6 of 12 trials at high overall risk of bias; weighing schedules and definitions of regain differed
inconsistency_reason: I² = 94%; the risk-of-bias subgroup difference is significant and driven by a single trial sitting on the null side
imprecision_reason: Only 347 infants; the effect loses significance under the Hartung-Knapp adjustment (p = 0.098) and when either of two trials is omitted
comments: A reduction of roughly 3 days is estimated from five small trials with near-complete heterogeneity; the finding is not robust to reasonable analytical choices.
